comment: Brian VO for 'WorldCup26 Bonus - Erling Haaland' (300s Viking-saga motivational film). VERIFIED facts (sources in README): 1066 Harald Hardrada sailed ~300 ships to conquer England, fell at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, only 24 ships returned home; Erling Haaland born 21 July 2000 in Leeds, England, while father Alf-Inge 'Alfie' Haaland played in the Premier League (Nottingham Forest, Leeds, Man City); Alfie's career ended early through injury; family returned to Bryne, Norway; Norway's first World Cup since 1998. The seer/witch, the voyage, the Wembley battle and the 2-1 scoreline are OUR STORY / OUR PREDICTION (labeled in VO line 30 and on-screen watermark). TONE: epic, mysterious, motivational. Battle = football only, no weapons combat, no gore. NO subtitles. Numbers spelled out for TTS.

lines.text: The old sagas tell of a seer in the far north... who made one promise. What the last king could not take... a son born on enemy soil would take for him.
One thousand years ago, three hundred Viking ships sailed out of Norway... to conquer England.
They fell at a place called Stamford Bridge. The king of Norway... the last great Viking... never came home.
Of three hundred ships, only twenty-four returned across the sea. And the north never forgot.
Now... did you know? In the year two thousand, inside England itself... in the city of Leeds... a Norwegian was born.
His father, Alfie Haaland, fought a decade in the Premier League. Nottingham Forest. Leeds. Manchester City.
But his father's battle ended too soon. An injury took his legs from under him... and a dream was left unfinished on English grass.
So the family sailed home. To Bryne. A small town of wind, rain... and iron will.
And there the boy grew. In the cold. Through the long dark winters. With one fire burning in his chest.
And the seer's promise followed him like a shadow. Born on enemy soil... destined to return.
Erling Braut Haaland. The goals stopped sounding human. Goal... after goal... after goal.
A machine, they called him. But machines do not dream. And this Viking dreamed of one shore.
Then the horn finally sounded. For the first time since nineteen ninety-eight... Norway reached the World Cup.
And from every fjord they came — the red army of the north, answering a thousand-year-old call.
The crew of the great red ship. Odegaard at the rudder. Sorloth. Nusa. Berge. Shoulder to shoulder.
And one word thundered across the North Sea. Ro! Ro! Ro! Row... for the twenty-four ships. Row... for the ones who never came home.
And on a cliff above the fjord, a father lit a candle... and prayed for his son to finish what he could not.
England was waiting. This is their fortress... and every fortress has a king.
Harry Kane. The captain. The record breaker. The king an entire island stands behind.
Bellingham. Rice. Foden. Saka. A wall of white. This crown will not be given... it must be taken.
So hear our story. The horns sound at Wembley... and the battle of the new Stamford Bridge begins.
And the king strikes first! Kane! One nil to England... and a thousand years of history starts laughing at the north all over again.
A thousand years of almost. Twenty-four ships. A father's unfinished dream. All of it... on one son's shoulders.
Then... through the storm... listen. Ro. Ro. Ro. The red army would not stop rowing.
Odegaard sees him. One pass. Haaland! The equalizer! The bridge is shaking!
And in the dying minutes... the seer's promise comes due. Haaland... again! Two, one!
The son born on English soil has taken what the last king could not. In our story... England falls to the north.
And high in the stands, a father closes his eyes. The prayer is answered. The dream is finished.
So whatever shore they tell you that you will never reach... row. Together. Ro! Ro! Ro!
Remember — this battle is our story, our prediction. Play yours free at WorldCup twenty-six dot world. Just for fun. No prizes.
Subscribe... and sail with us. Skol!
